title: add benchmark-lab representative runners and reporting pipeline v86
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: bring a new set of representative workload runners into benchmark-lab and wire them into the v86 reporting pipeline. This PR adds a family of runners that model latency-sensitive conversational workloads and short-prompt embedding workloads, plus the reporting pipeline to aggregate perf and profiling baselines. The change is split into: runner harnesses, workload definitions, Prometheus + tracing hooks, reporting pipeline templates (pipeline_v86.yaml), CI workflows, and README/docs updates.

Scope and summary: - Add representative_runner.py harness with configurable arrival processes (poisson, bursty, steady) and KV-cache warmup helpers. - Add embedding_runner.py for short prompt/embedding-heavy workloads. - Add pipeline_v86.yaml which collects run metadata, perf metrics (p50/p90/p99), token-level cost breakdown, and profiling baselines (GPU memory, kernel times). - Instrument runners with prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry spans. - Add end-to-end tests that run a tiny local DAG and assert reporting artifacts are written. - Add CI job (infra/ci/benchmark-lab.yml) to run subset of workloads on PRs and the full pipeline on main branch nightly.

Testing and validation: unit tests included for arrival generator and KV-warmup logic. Local e2e harness verifies full pipeline on a single small instance and writes artifacts to test-bucket. CI: a flaky test in e2e was stabilized by increasing timeout and adding retry; CI passed on final run. Benchmarks: ran representative runs against local dev models and verified that reported p90 latency improvements after adaptive-batching changes remain within expected variance.

Related: Linear ENG-6123 (benchmark-lab v86), ENG-5984 (adaptive-batching followups). See docs/benchmark-lab/README.md for usage and config knobs.

Notes: this PR is intentionally conservative in runtime changes (no changes to serving runtime internals). Runner code lives entirely in benchmark-lab and reporting pipeline is backward compatible with v85 artifacts.

review_comments: Diego: Can we make arrival distro configurable via env var instead of hardcoded? Requested change: expose --arrival and add unit test.
Maya: Addressed in 8c2d4e1, added CLI flag and unit test. PTAL.

Maya: Increased timeout to 90s and added retry wrapper; CI green on rerun.
Ravi: Approved, minor nits in README fixed in final commit.
summary_of_changes: Introduces two new representative runners (conversational and embedding patterns), instruments metrics and traces, and adds a v86 reporting pipeline that aggregates performance and profiling baselines. Adds CI coverage and docs updates.
testing_notes: Unit tests for arrival generator and KV warmup; local e2e harness available at benchmark-lab/tests/e2e with a Docker compose recipe for a single-node run. CI runs a smoke e2e on PRs and the full nightly pipeline on main. Flaky e2e stabilized by adding retry and extended timeout.
release_notes: Add benchmark-lab v86: representative workload runners (conversational + embedding), v86 reporting pipeline, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry tracing, CI workflow. No serving runtime changes.
notes: This is a repo-scoped feature in benchmark-lab; recommended follow-ups are a dashboard in observability-pack for v86 artifacts and a scheduled nightly comparison job for regressions.
